records.name: Świętokrzyskie Voivodeship
records.summary:
Świętokrzyskie was the fifth of the voivodeships adopting a regional "anti-LGBT ideology" resolution by June 2020, completing the configuration that at peak covered about a third of national territory across roughly 100 municipalities and five regions. Located in the same eastern conservative bloc as Łódzkie and Lubelskie, its resolution was annulled or repealed in the 2020–2021 court-and-EU-pressure wave.

No march ban, violence episode, or holdout municipality comparable to the Subcarpathian or Podlaskie findings is documented at the voivodeship scale. The visitor-facing signal is the regional declaration's intent to exclude LGBTQ public presence and the social climate of the PiS heartland belt; the formal legal document is now absent.

Score of 0.48 sits 0.04 below the national 0.52, identical to Łódzkie (0.48) on shared evidence: both are resolution-carrying voivodeships in the eastern bloc without unit-specific enforcement or violence findings beyond the declaration itself. sources.summary: Per-voivodeship revocation record: the Supreme Administrative Court of Poland revoked Łódź Voivodeship's anti-LGBT resolution on 12 October 2023, and the Świętokrzyskie voivodeship council revoked its own resolution on 22 September 2021 (the European Commission had written to the governors of five voivodeships — Lublin, Łódź, Lesser Poland, Podkarpackie, and Świętokrzyskie — on 2 June 2020 about the resolutions). By 24 April 2025 all anti-LGBTQ resolutions and all Local Government Family Rights Charters in Poland had been withdrawn or invalidated by court order.

Between 2019 and 2025 more than 100 Polish local governments adopted ‘LGBT-free zone’-style resolutions which at their peak covered roughly a third of the country's land area; Polish administrative courts struck them down as unconstitutional (Article 32 equal treatment), the European Commission linked EU development funds to their repeal, and the last remaining zone (in Łańcut) was abolished in 2025. The article notes the resolutions were symbolic and institutional rather than criminal — they created no new penalties and barred no one physically — but signalled to local bureaucracies and schools which families and identities local leadership considered legitimate.

records.name: Masovian Voivodeship
records.summary:
Masovian, anchored by Warsaw, is the institutional counterweight to Poland's eastern resolution belt. On 6 February 2024, Warsaw's Voivodeship Administrative Court repealed the last remaining "against LGBT ideology" document in the country. Warsaw is the origin point of the progressive response: in February 2019 Mayor Rafał Trzaskowski signed a 12-point LGBT+ Declaration (security, education, culture, sport, employment; drawn up with LGBT NGOs, including an intervention hostel and school "lighthouse keeper" projects), which provoked the first anti-LGBT municipal resolution (Świdnik, March 2019) as an explicit counter-reaction. The administrative-court campaign, led from Warsaw by the national Commissioner for Human Rights and carried through the provincial administrative courts and the Supreme Administrative Court, dismantled the resolution network nationally.

sources.summary: Wikipedia's consolidated 'LGBT-free zone' overview records the full arc: by January 2020 a third of Poland's territory had passed anti-LGBT resolutions; on 6 February 2024 Warsaw's Voivodeship Administrative Court repealed the last document 'against LGBT ideology' in Poland; by 24 April 2025 every anti-LGBTQ resolution and Family Charter endorsement was withdrawn or court-invalidated.

URBACT's March 2019 account of Warsaw's LGBT+ Declaration: Mayor Trzaskowski signed the capital's pledge of equality, non-discrimination and hate-crime response, and the piece documents the declaration's politics and reception in Warsaw — the 2019 commitment freshness confirms shows no record of repeal.
